title: "About"
---

## Purpose

Chemical engineering has an unusually rich stock of phenomenological models —
Thiele's effectiveness factor, Kunii–Levenspiel's bubbling bed, the
Doyle–Fuller–Newman battery model — that are taught everywhere and reimplemented
constantly, usually from scratch and usually without the original data at hand.

This gallery collects them in one place, each reproduced with `pymrm` and shown
against the experimental data it was validated on, as a runnable notebook.

## The page contract

Every page shows the same four things, in the same order:

1. the model **as originally published**, in the original notation, with a table
   mapping symbols to code variables;
2. the **core experimental data**, as a plain CSV with a machine-readable
   provenance sidecar;
3. the **pymrm reproduction** overlaid on that data, with a quantitative
   agreement metric that CI tracks for regressions;
4. **what pymrm adds** — and if it adds nothing, the page says so. A faithful
   reproduction is a legitimate result; a manufactured improvement is not.

Every page also carries at least one validation that does not use the
experimental data: an analytical limit, a conservation check, or a
grid/time-step independence check.

## Classification

Two axes. **Physical domain** (`sec:`) is what you browse. **Mathematical
structure** (`struct:`) is what you reuse — codes `S1`–`S13` describing the
shape of the numerical problem rather than the physics. Pages sharing a
structure code are solved by nearly the same pymrm code even when their subject
matter is unrelated, which is the intended route to adapting a model from
outside your own field.

Full scheme: [`docs/taxonomy.md`](https://github.com/pymrm/pymrm-gallery/blob/main/docs/taxonomy.md).

## Licensing

| Component | Licence |
|---|---|
| Code — notebooks, `shared/`, `scripts/` | MIT |
| Prose and figures generated here | CC-BY-4.0 |
| Data we generate ourselves | CC0 |
| Data digitised from third-party publications | not relicensed — see below |

Digitised datasets are distributed as **factual data with attribution**.
Numerical values are facts and are not protected by copyright; extraction for
scientific research by a research organisation with lawful access is covered by
Art. 15n of the Dutch Auteurswet, implementing Art. 3 of the DSM Directive (EU)
2019/790. Source figure images are never reproduced — points are re-plotted from
extracted coordinates — and source PDFs are never committed. Each dataset's
`.meta.yaml` records its origin, extraction method, and basis for
redistribution.

If you are an author whose data appears here and you would like a page changed
or removed, please open an issue; we will act on it promptly.

## Relationship to the rest of PyMRM

- [`pymrm`](https://github.com/multiscale-modelling-multiphase-flows/pymrm) —
  the library itself.
- `pymrm-book` — the course book: tutorials, exercises, and lecture notes for
  the Multiphase Reactor Modeling course at TU Eindhoven.
- **this gallery** — validated reproductions of published models, for research
  reuse rather than teaching.

The book teaches you the method. The gallery gives you a model to start from.

## Citing

Cite **both** the original publication and this gallery. Each page lists its
primary reference; the gallery itself has a `CITATION.cff` and a DOI per
release.
